issues.legal_issue: For an execution proceeding involving a final, unconditional partition decree, limitation begins when the decree is enforceable, not when it is later engrossed on stamp paper.
material_facts: A final partition decree determined the parties’ shares and left no substantive matter for later adjudication.
The court directed the decree-holders to provide stamp paper, but they did not do so within the time allowed.
Providing the stamp paper was within the decree-holders’ control, and the execution application was filed more than twelve years after the decree was passed.
issues.conclusion: The decree was enforceable from the date it was passed, and the later failure to provide stamp paper did not postpone the commencement of limitation. The execution application was therefore time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 of the Limitation Act, 1963 runs from when a decree becomes enforceable. Enforceability is distinct from executability: where a final decree has determined the rights and the court has not postponed enforcement or made it conditional on an external event, a later ministerial step controlled by the decree-holder does not suspend limitation. The Court applied Yeswant Deorao Deshmukh v. Watch and Ramchand Kothari and W.B. Essential Commodities Supply Corporation v. Swadesh Agro Farming and Storage Pvt. Ltd.; it distinguished Shankar Balwant Lokhande v. Chandrakant Shankar Lokhande because that case concerned a preliminary decree without a final decree, and relied on Biswapati Dev v. Kennsington Stores and Kishori Mohan Pal v. Pravash Chandra Mondal for the literal meaning of enforceability.

rule.if: decree_execution_proceeding and final_partition_decree_passed and rights_fully_determined and enforcement_not_postponed_by_court and decree_holder_controlled_stamp_filing

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding: The decree-holder sought to enforce a civil court decree through an execution proceeding.
predicates.final_partition_decree_passed: The court passed a final decree determining the division of property.
predicates.rights_fully_determined: The decree settled the parties’ rights without leaving a substantive matter for later adjudication.
predicates.enforcement_not_postponed_by_court: The court did not make enforcement conditional on a later event or expressly postpone it.
predicates.decree_holder_controlled_stamp_filing: The decree-holder could provide the stamp paper required for formal preparation of the decree but failed or delayed in doing so.

issues.definition: When an execution proceeding concerns a final partition decree that fully determines rights and whose enforcement was not postponed by the court, a stamp-paper step controlled by the decree-holder does not change the point from which limitation runs.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory restriction on acting upon an unstamped partition decree does not suspend limitation for executing the decree.
material_facts: The final partition decree had been passed, but the decree-holders had not supplied the stamp paper needed to engross it.
The decree-holders argued that the restriction on acting upon an unstamped instrument prevented the decree from being enforceable until it was engrossed.
The stamp-paper requirement was a formal step, and the decree-holders controlled whether and when to complete it.
issues.conclusion: The Stamp Act restriction did not suspend limitation; the period ran from when the final decree became enforceable, notwithstanding that it had not yet been engrossed on stamp paper.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 of the Limitation Act, 1963 governs the commencement of limitation for execution, while Sections 2(15) and 35 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 address partition instruments and the admissibility or use of unstamped instruments. The Court held that the Stamp Act’s restriction does not govern when limitation begins under Article 136 or override its mandate. It disapproved Bholanath Karmakar v. Madanmohan Karmakar, which had treated engrossment as postponing limitation, and distinguished Shankar Balwant Lokhande as a case in which no final decree had been passed.

rule.if: decree_execution_proceeding and final_partition_decree_passed and decree_not_yet_engrossed and stamp_formality_restricts_use_of_decree and decree_holder_controls_stamp_filing

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding: The decree-holder sought to enforce a civil court decree through an execution proceeding.
predicates.final_partition_decree_passed: The court passed a final decree determining the division of property.
predicates.decree_not_yet_engrossed: The final decree had not yet been formally engrossed on stamp paper.
predicates.stamp_formality_restricts_use_of_decree: A stamp-related requirement restricted the decree’s admission or use until the required formality was completed.
predicates.decree_holder_controls_stamp_filing: The decree-holder could provide the stamp paper required for formal preparation of the decree but failed or delayed in doing so.

issues.definition: When a decree-holder seeks execution of a final partition decree that remains unengrossed because of a stamp-paper formality within the decree-holder’s control, that formality does not pause limitation.
